tl;dr: A free-to-play asymmetric co-op puzzle game that is worth wasting an hour or two with, even if you can't play it in VR.

We Were Here doesn't really have any story, it simply puts you and your co-player in two different areas of a frozen castle and lets go of your hand. Which is perfectly fine. There is simply something enjoyable in having to exchange information with a friend in order to solve puzzles, no matter how easy or basic in their conception these puzzles may end up being. It's also entertaining to listen to a friend freaking out over seeing something mildly creepy, while all you're doing is patiently pressing levers in a completely different room with no idea what you're doing or what it is they're freaking out about.

There were still some kinks the game hadn't ironed out yet at the time of writing. Most important ones: The ingame chat didn't work (we used steam chat to play instead) and I got stuck in location at some point, having to wait till I died to be able to restart the puzzle. And frankly it's not a particularly pretty game, in fact it feels like your standard unity game in a rather obvious way. But it does have some creepy moments here and there, and there is a segment in a frozen yard that was equal parts annoying and nicely immersive. I also laughed maniacly at the ending, for reasons I will not spoil for you. 

All in all, it's just plain ol' good fun, and the rough edges are forgiveable for a free game. So if you're still waiting for [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/341800]Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes[/url] to get a deeper discount, this game should help scratch a similar itch for free. Just find a buddy to play with, and make sure to set aside those 1-2 hours, because despite having checkpoints to allow for toilet breaks and drink refills, there is no real save system. 

Looking forward to more from these devs.

We Were Here was not great. It's free, so you can't really complain, but also, I can, and I will. 

Firstly, for the few positives, the beginning and ending cinematics were very beautiful and immersive, and the music throughout the experience was generally decent and pleasant to listen to.

Now for the negatives, which is basically everything else.

There are two roles; the explorer and the reader. You never deviate from these roles; the explorer is always doing, and the reader is always reading. This is exhausting for the explorer, and boring for the reader. The experience and pacing of this game are completely different for both players, and it's not replayable because many of the puzzles rely on you having no knowledge of their solutions.

I say "many" of the puzzles, but I really mean about half. The other half are entirely solvable without any cooperation. Yes, you read me right. Half of the puzzles in this asymetrical co-op experience are solvable without communication. Progress relies on the explorer beating the puzzle, with no required input from the reader other than information. This means that many of the puzzles are very easily brute forced, with no need to consult the reader for any information; oftentimes, the information is simply available to the explorer, and no extra work is needed. There is a maze that requires no assistance from the reader, there are combination locks and paths that can be solved with basic trial and error that don't even take more than 5 minutes entirely alone; its so bizarre to me that the developers didn't think about this obvious and glaring flaw, as it invalidates the appeal of an experience that is supposed to be a fun puzzle solving game between two people.

Also, there are randomly time limits on many of the puzzles. This is odd, as the time limits don't really "punish" you as much as they simply inconvenience you. They just reset the puzzle. That's it. So if you have been stuck on a part of a puzzle for a while, and then you die, you have to tediously get through all the parts you already know how to solve, just to get back to the part that was giving you trouble. Why? This doesn't make any sense and is purely tedious for the sake of it. 

Also, the story kind of fails to be compelling. Spoilers below. 

[spoiler] It hooks you pretty well with the intro; two individuals wandering through a snowy landscape find a castle. They enter and are knocked out and separated by a mysterious entity, who presumably is the one forcing them to do these bizarre puzzles to escape. This eventually ends with one of the characters being left behind. This creates lots of questions; why is there a castle in the middle of nowhere? Why is there an entity who traps these people? What were these people doing out here in the first place? And why is one left behind? Literally none of these questions are answered in any capacity, which fails to leave any significant emotional impact. We don't relate to or care about these characters at all. [/spoiler]

Finally, the visuals past the cinematics are kind of... not great looking. In particular, there is an unfinished pipe asset in one of the early rooms, and the chess pieces in the courtyard are clearly very simple polygonal blender models. The symbols were very unique and cool, but barely utilized in the cooperative play, which is a huge missed opportunity.

At the end of the day, this is free and clearly early project from this studio, but it's still pretty bad even for a first go. I give it grace for it's efforts, and hope that the next few titles are improvements on the formula!

[hr][/hr]
I played [b]We Were Here[/b] with the same person I later played through the rest of the series with, and even the first game immediately won us over. The basic concept is simple but incredibly effective: you are separated from each other and can only communicate via radio. This constantly creates situations where you have to explain things to each other without actually knowing exactly what the other person is seeing.

What we especially enjoyed was how important communication really is. You can't just run around quickly or rely on knowing a solution from the internet. You have to listen, communicate clearly, and figure things out together. Especially when playing with someone you get along well with, this can be incredibly fun.

We also really liked the atmosphere of the castle. The environment feels mysterious and, at times, even a little creepy, without constantly relying on cheap jumpscares. Instead, the game creates tension through isolation and the unfamiliar surroundings.

Of course, you can tell in some places that this is the first game and that it doesn't have as much content as the later entries. For us, though, that wasn't a problem at all. On the contrary, it works wonderfully as an introduction to the series.

For two players who enjoy solving puzzles together and can laugh about their own communication mistakes along the way, I can definitely recommend [b]We Were Here[/b]. For us, it was the perfect start to a really great co-op series.

[h1]We Were Here - A Thrilling Co-op Puzzle Adventure![/h1]

I had a lot of fun playing [i]We Were Here[/i] with my friend (profile link). It was an amazing experience, and I'm excited to play the other games in the series since I own them all. I played using a keyboard, and it was a scary but fun game. I'm grateful my buddy tried to play with me, and we had so much fun. This game is perfect for multiplayer, so you'll definitely want a friend to play with you. I wouldn't recommend playing on public servers.

[h2]Gameplay and Mechanics:[/h2]
The gameplay in [i]We Were Here[/i] is very exciting and challenging. You and your friend are separated in an abandoned castle and must communicate using walkie-talkies to solve puzzles and escape. Each player has a different view and experience, making communication and cooperation essential. The puzzles are well-designed and require teamwork to solve, which adds to the excitement and fun of the game.

[h2]Graphics and Performance:[/h2]

The environments are well-designed, with lots of details that add to the eerie feeling of the game. The sound effects and music also contribute to the immersive experience, making the game even more thrilling.

[h2]Controls:[/h2]
I played [i]We Were Here[/i] using a keyboard, and it worked very well. The controls are easy to learn and very responsive. Moving around, interacting with objects, and communicating with your partner feel natural and smooth. The game also supports customizable controls, so you can set them up to fit your preferences. The tutorial is helpful and teaches you the basics quickly, making it easy to get started.

[h2]Multiplayer Experience:[/h2]
Playing [i]We Were Here[/i] with a friend is the best way to enjoy the game. The multiplayer mode allows you to team up and solve puzzles together. Communicating and coordinating with your friend adds a lot of fun and excitement. The game is designed for cooperative play, and having a dedicated partner makes the experience much more enjoyable. Playing on public servers is not recommended, as it can be hard to find committed players.

[h2]Replayability and Content:[/h2]

The developers have created a series of games, so there are more adventures to look forward to. Each game in the series builds on the previous one, adding new puzzles and challenges. The community is also very supportive, with many players sharing tips and custom content to enhance the game.

[h2]Overall:[/h2]
[i]We Were Here[/i] is a fantastic co-op puzzle game. It is fun, challenging, and very entertaining. If you enjoy puzzle games and playing with friends, you should definitely try this game. It's one of the best cooperative games I've played, and I highly recommend it. The mix of puzzles, communication, and teamwork, combined with the great multiplayer experience, makes this game a must-play. Whether you are a fan of puzzle games or just looking for something fun to play with friends, [i]We Were Here[/i] offers hours of entertainment. The developers have created a truly engaging experience that is worth exploring with a friend.

i really love this game and the series its apart of, but this one for sure takes the gold. its got the right amount of spooky, lore bits, and challenging puzzles. i love the mechanic of the walkie-talkies, its nice that theres a built in vc so you can interact with people who arent on a discord or skype call. all in all one of my favorites, highly recommend

its a fun game for a couple hours. we got 100% achievements in just less than 3 hours. bought all 5 games on sale for about £15 so the short playtime doesn't feel like a waste. worth buying the collection in a sale for sure but don't go into it expecting extended longevity. after your first play through you can easily complete the game a second time in about 15 minutes.

Whole series of [Great] Co-op games, some might be better some might be shorter, but they follow the same formula of communication and cooperation. Buying a bundle and going through the whole series with a friend is Incredible fun.
Great opening to the series! We were able to knock out all achievements in about 4 and a half hours. Highly recommend to couples that enjoy puzzles!

Got thrown off by the pseudo-horror stuff (unlisted in genre/tag) during the theatre puzzle room - also the game has a few issues with readability and UI which make the game less fun and more frustrating to play

I was glad to have had the opportunity to try the original We Were Here with a good friend over this past weekend. I love escape rooms and have been intrigued about this series as it had come highly recommended in a games for education group.

Long story short, conceptually, the pieces are here for creating a memorable co-op escape room experience, but at least here in the original, the execution falls flat in a few of the puzzle scenarios. I really hope that this was just the first step towards a greater vision that the designers learned a lot from and that the later installments make significant improvements. I doubt the game would have come so highly recommended to me if this was the only one out there. It's not bad per se - this one just needed a little more time in the oven.

Absolutely love this game! The graphics and mechanics in this first one can be a bit janky/frustrating at times, but it's still a fun play, especially with a friend or partner! Highly recommend this entire series!
Great game I played with my best friend and we got divorced eventually. (only negative there is no sex to avoid arguments)
This is a fast and cheap game that I recommend for a fun teamworking exercise. It is relatively fast so I recommend getting it bundled or when it is on sale. Overall like a 6/10 experience.

Are you looking to start your Steam gaming experience with a free game? Look no further than We Were Here. An escape room, co-op,  puzzle game that will have your brain put to work while surviving the horrors that await you...

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED YOU PLAY WITH A FRIEND AND HAVE A MIC!!!

The game is extremely buggy, couldn't progress with a friend past the first set of puzzles.  There is a projector that you need to attach a reel of film to that dictates actions that your partner needs to take.  This projector will not work 100% of the time, I got it to work once, but had to quit before we could finish the puzzle.  Resumed at a later date and was unable to get the projector to work, and player two was unable to move the pieces that should have been shown on the projector. This is a pretty good tutorial for the other games, but the librarian role is pretty boring. Which is fine due to it's short length and definitely still worth playing.
This game was challenging but a lot of fun. I'm just glad I was in house with my teammate though since a lot of the pictures were very similar.

This is a fun little puzzle game where you do need a coop partner.

The idea is that you are trapped in two different parts of this mysterious castle and each has a solution or aid to assist the other person to get through their puzzle. (eg. one may be stuck in a maze with levers to operate and the other has the map and can see the colour of the doors)

It is a short game, so it is a quick experience, especially worth a quick run amongst friends. However several of the puzzles remain the same during each run, so once you have seen them, the novelty is lost.

Overall tho, I do recommend getting this, and maybe looking at the other games in the series (this is the first one).
Good escape simulating series. If you like these puzzle-escape kind of games, you will defenitely like this one with a friend.

This is a great puzzle game! Now I'm going to say that again, it's a PUZZLE GAME. All the reviews saying you have to cheat to figure out how to play... completely false. They are puzzles. The fun of the game is in figuring out how to help each other. It has moments that are frustrating and really put your mind to the test. Some are so simple that you completely overlook the answer, where others are real thinkers. The librarian is fun because they're in control and their analytic skills lead the game. The explorer gets more of the visual adventure but they are completely reliant on their partner. Either way both characters are great and I can't wait to continue this series.

*All Achievements Achieved*

I've played this game with 3 different friends the 1st took 2.5 hours and was stressful, the 2nd gave up at the paintings room because he couldn't describe the symbols at all, and the 3rd I played with made me feel like we were speed runners, this game really shows who has a brain and who doesn't.

Don't be fooled by my playtime, I have played this on a different platform before. This game and its sequels are one my most favorite game series out there. The puzzles are fun and really test your communication skills. It's simple to understand and yet challenging. a great experience all around and if you enjoy it, every following game gets even better. Super awesome game! It was so fun to play, that it was the first game I attempted to speedrun. We are posting our score tonight. Highly recommend.
Quick game, good for a rainy afternoon. Puzzles were very well done and intuitive, so we didn't have to look up a guide to get through it. Story was very intriguing

It's a decent co-op puzzler. The puzzles are not too difficult and they seem to be there just for their own sake as I couldn't really see any story elements. Some bugs and short. But it's free, so there's nothing to lose.

Amazing Puzzles, very lightly buggy at times, for example the chess pieces can be wonky, and the books sometimes float but for a free game this was only but a little annoyance. I would even be happy if I payed a little money for this game. So since it is free you have nothing to lose but a sweet little game to play with a friend. Really fun!!!
First game of an amazing trilogy (soon 4). Free and worth trying out [b] with a friend [/b]. Nobody should ever try one of WWH games with a random person, because communication is key and it can be infuriating at time when you don't get the solution.

Everyone who likes coop games and/or puzzle games should try this game.
(Keep in mind, this is the first game of the series, so it only gets better from here)
Played with my girlfriend. Fun puzzle adventure that requires good communication. DEFINITELY worth a play through with it being free.

Super fun game, though that may depend on your friend. FYI you can not save and quit so you have to dedicate about an hour to beat the game. My friend and I beat it in 25 - 30ish mins but we do puzzle game a lot together. 100% can be done in 2 runs but we missed a secret achievement so it took us 4 runs.

This game is wonderful. It is a short puzzle game and given that it is free I would advise anybody to pick it up just to play even if they don't end up going into the series. But I do have to say they are so worth the money.

Quite short but still nice cooperation game. It is good one if you want to do something simple, but still interesting. Some of puzzles also can be challenging. It depends on good cooperation to finish quick or bed one -  to die again and again.  

You need to take one of two possible roles: Explorer or Librarian. You don't see each other and can only use in-game device to voice chat. Each of you have your own "territory" where hits can be found. Speaking and discussing what each of you see helps to understand puzzle and go to the next one. 

Also, there is a time restriction. If you stay on  one puzzle for too long you'll die. But you can still start again from the last checkpoint. There is no manual saving option. 

So, game is short and highly depends on players team work. But still quite fun even if you have a so-so cooperation. Recommend to try is yourself.

Fun short puzzle game for two.

My husband and I played  this game together. In 2.8 hours we were able to go through the game twice, so we could each play as both roles.

The atmosphere is slightly creepy, but not so creepy that you would lose sleep over it. (Which I personally like a lot.)

The controls are solid. The visuals are very basic (though I really appreciated the dog portraits), but in my opinion, that doesn't really matter for this type of game.
